entities.summary:
Peter González Telmo, known posthumously as Saint Elmo, emerged as a pivotal figure in the religious landscape of 13th-century Castile, embodying the dynamic spiritual renewal characteristic of the High Middle Ages. Born in Frómista, Palencia, in 1190, he rose from a privileged ecclesiastical background to become a zealous Dominican friar and confessor to King Ferdinand III of Castile, playing a crucial role in the moral and spiritual guidance of the nascent Reconquista efforts. His life and ministry profoundly influenced the Castilian court and populace, particularly through his dedication to preaching and charitable works among the marginalized and the seafaring communities of the Iberian Peninsula.

Initially groomed for a comfortable ecclesiastical career through the patronage of his uncle, Bishop Tello Téllez de Meneses of Palencia, González underwent a profound spiritual conversion after a public humiliation. He renounced his prebendary status, joined the recently established Dominican Order, and dedicated himself to itinerant preaching, particularly in the regions of Asturias, Galicia, and Portugal. As King Ferdinand III's confessor, he accompanied the monarch on several campaigns of the Reconquista, including the sieges of Seville and Córdoba, where he ministered to soldiers and captives, offering spiritual counsel and advocating for humane treatment of the conquered Muslim populations.
